summary: 13th Dalai Lama (1876–1933) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under teachers including Terton Sogyal, Agvan Dorzhiev, Pa Ri Rabsal, and Yeshe Chopel, and taught numerous disciples, including Rangjung Rigpe Dorje and Jamphel Yeshe Gyaltsen.

The 14th Dalai Lama (born 1935) works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He studied under teachers including Trijang Rinpoche, Ling Rinpoche, Tsenshab Serkong Rinpoche, Khunu Rinpoche, Dilgo Khyentse, and Trulshik Rinpoche, and founded the International Network of Engaged Buddhists (1989).

14th Dalai Lama Tenzin Gyatso (born 1935) specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied under teachers including Heinrich Harrer, Jamphel Yeshe Gyaltsen, Tagdrag Rinpoche, Ling Rinpoche, and Trijang Rinpoche, and founded the Mind and Life Institute in 1990.

19th Kushok Bakula Rinpoche (1917–2003) worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied under Jamphel Yeshe Gyaltsen, Ngawang Lobzang Gyatso, and Khangsar Dorje Chang (~1930–1941).

The 3rd Sras Rinpoche (born 1937) is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under the 96th Ganden Tripa Thubten Kunga, at Drepung Loseling Monastery (1950–1971), and at Gyume Tantric College (1971), later holding posts at both institutions.

The 5th Samdhong Rinpoche Lobsang Tenzin (born 1939) works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Drepung Monastery (~1951–1959) and held posts at the Central School for Tibetans (1960–1970) and Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (1971–2001).

id: P:7th Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche Karma Sungrab Ngedön Tenpe Gyeltshen
summary: The 7th Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche Karma Sungrab Ngedön Tenpe Gyeltshen (born 1965) works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He served as director of the Kamalashila Institute and founded Nitartha International and Nalandabodhi.

A. A. Krishnaswami Ayyangar (1892–1953) studied at Pachaiyappa's College (~1908–1911). He later worked at Pachaiyappa's College (1911–1918) and served as a professor at the University of Mysore (1918–1947).
A. B. Gajendragadkar was an Indologist. He held positions as Senior Dakshina Fellow at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute and as Lecturer on Sanskrit at Karnatak Arts College.

A. Charles Muller (born 1953) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and computational fields. He earned his PhD at Stony Brook University under Sung Bae Park and held posts at Toyo Gakuen University, the University of Tokyo, and Musashino University.

A. F. Rudolf Hoernle (1841–1918) was a scholar in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He served as director at Aliah University (~1881–1895) and as secretary of the Asiatic Society in 1891.
A. G. Mohan (born 1945) is an Indologist who studied under Tirumalai Krishnamacharya from circa 1971 to 1989. He founded the Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandiram in 1976.

A. K. Ramanujan (1929–1993) worked in Indology and linguistics. He earned degrees from Maharaja's College, Mysore, and Indiana University Bloomington, and held a long-term professorship at the University of Chicago from 1962, alongside a visiting post at Harvard.

A. K. Warder (1924–2013) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his doctorate at SOAS under John Brough (~1950–1954) and held posts at the University of Edinburgh (1955–1963) and the University of Toronto (1963–1990).
A. N. Krishna Aiyangar was an Indologist. He held posts as Joint Editor of Brahmavidyā: The Adyar Library Bulletin (attested 1942) and at the Adyar Library and Research Centre (attested 1940–1942).

A. N. Narasimhia worked in linguistics and Indology. He completed a PhD at SOAS University of London under Ralph Lilley Turner (~1930–1933) and held posts at the University of Mysore and Maharaja's College, Mysore.
A. W. Barber is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He completed a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1984 and held an attested post at the University of Calgary in 1998.

Aaron P. Proffitt is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He earned his PhD at the University of Michigan under Micah L. Auerback and became an assistant professor of Japanese Studies at the University at Albany, SUNY, around 2015.
Abaji Vishnu Kathavate was an Indologist who succeeded Ramakrishna Gopal Bhandarkar. He held the post of Professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 2026).

Abanindranath Tagore (1871–1951) was an Indologist and art historian. He studied at Sanskrit Collegiate School, Sanskrit College and University, and Government College of Art & Craft, and served at the University of Calcutta (~1921–1929).
